name: African mango (Irvingia gabonensis)
short: In systematic reviews of 3 to 5 trials, reported adverse events were minor and included headache and sleep difficulty; the trials were poorly reported, so safety data are limited.
text: A systematic review of three randomised trials of Irvingia gabonensis for weight loss reported that adverse events included headache and sleep difficulty, and noted that all three trials had flaws in the reporting of their methods. A later systematic review and meta-analysis of five randomised trials of the seed extract described the reported adverse events as minor, while rating four of the five trials at high risk of bias and noting insufficient reporting. In a 90-day study in rats, a seed kernel extract produced no toxicologically significant treatment-related changes at any dose tested; this is animal data and does not establish safety in people. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
